evidence_items.explanation: A choice experiment involving 314 US adults found substantial willingness to choose paid plans with suitable features. It challenges an inference from nonpayment to unwillingness, but its geography, hypothetical choices and earlier fieldwork prevent a decisive assessment.

The study reports that 2.9% of US consumers paid for at least one of four major providers in April. This supports limited paid adoption in that sample and month, but does not measure willingness to pay or compute-customer affordability.

unresolved_gaps: No readable, representative willingness-to-pay measurement covering the claimed population and target quarter was established.
No representative denominator or financial dataset establishes the share of paying compute customers unable to afford their purchases.
Earlier payment data cannot establish present unwillingness, and selected loss-making buyers cannot establish an overwhelming majority.
